growth_story.headline: Iran's income per person is still 24.3 percent below its 1976 peak, after revolution, war with Iraq, sanctions and now a new conflict.
growth_story.arc: Income per person in Iran peaked in 1976 and fell through the revolution and the war with Iraq; in 2025 it was still 24.3 percent below that peak, about where it first stood in 1971. From 1990 to 2007 it grew 3.2 percent a year, as the oil sector recovered somewhat from the war and oil prices rose sharply from 1999. The IMF says that in the decade before the 2012 sanctions Iran's income moved closer to richer countries' levels, mostly because it added capital and workers. From 2008 to 2025 the average fell to 0.6 percent a year: the IMF links the sharp fall after 2012 to sanctions that cut oil output and productivity, and the World Bank reported in 2024 that oil output was still well below its level before US sanctions returned in 2018. Growth rose to 1.3 percent a year over 2016–2025, from 0.7 in 2006–2015, carried by steady growth from 2020 to 2024. Income per person then fell 3.7 percent in 2025, the year of a short war with Israel, and the World Bank describes a 2026 conflict that has damaged the country's productive capacity.

threads.title: Revolution, war and oil collapse
threads.text: In the 1970s oil made up a large part of the economy. Oil output fell sharply after the 1979 revolution, and the war with Iraq damaged oil facilities. Income per person in the data fell in most years from 1977 to 1988.

citations.title: Islamic Republic of Iran: Selected Issues (IMF Country Report No. 08/285)

citations.title: Islamic Republic of Iran: Selected Issues (IMF Country Report No. 08/285)

threads.title: Oil boom and catch-up
threads.text: The 1990–2007 era ended in a long rise in oil prices. The IMF says that in the decade before the 2012 sanctions Iran's income moved closer to richer countries' levels, mostly because it added capital and workers.

citations.title: Islamic Republic of Iran: Selected Issues (IMF Country Report No. 08/285)

citations.title: Islamic Republic of Iran: 2015 Article IV Consultation—Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director

threads.title: Sanctions since 2012
threads.text: The IMF says the sanctions tightened in 2012 pushed productivity growth below zero and cut oil output and exports. In 2024 the World Bank reported oil output still well below its level before US sanctions returned in 2018, and the IMF lists sanctions among the causes of Iran's rising inflation in 2025.

citations.title: Islamic Republic of Iran: 2015 Article IV Consultation—Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director
citations.quote: The intensification of sanctions pushed TFP growth into negative territory and led to sharp contractions in production and exports in the hydrocarbon sector.

citations.title: Iran Economic Monitor: Sustaining Growth Amid Rising Geopolitical Tensions (Spring 2024)
citations.quote: Despite this recovery, oil production remains well below the pre-sanctions high of an average of 3.8 mbpd in 2017 and the first half of 2018.

citations.title: Regional Economic Outlook: Middle East and Central Asia, October 2025 — Resilience amid Uncertainty: Will it Last?
citations.quote: The Islamic Republic of Iran remained an outlier, with inflation rising because of exchange rate pressures, loose monetary and fiscal policies, and international sanctions.

threads.title: Long strains on living standards
threads.text: The World Bank says high inflation, low investment and instability wore down living standards over decades. It also finds that most working-age Iranians do not have jobs and that youth unemployment has stayed high for two decades. In 2024 it noted that several years of growth had not closed the gap with peer countries.

citations.title: Iran, Islamic Republic: Macro Poverty Outlook (October 2026)
citations.quote: Decades of economic mismanagement, chronic underinvestment, and macroeconomic instability had eroded living standards.

citations.title: Iran, Islamic Republic: Macro Poverty Outlook (October 2026)
citations.quote: Only 24.8 million of 66.1 million working-age Iranians were employed, with youth unemployment above 20 percent for two decades

citations.title: Iran Economic Monitor: Sustaining Growth Amid Rising Geopolitical Tensions (Spring 2024)
citations.quote: However, despite the economic expansion over the last four years, Iran has yet to bridge the gap with its peer groups

threads.title: War in 2025 and 2026
threads.text: A short war with Israel in June 2025 was followed by a conflict in 2026. The World Bank reports damage to energy, industry and transport, and income per person in the data fell 3.7 percent in 2025.

citations.title: Regional Economic Outlook: Middle East and Central Asia, October 2025 — Resilience amid Uncertainty: Will it Last?

since_last_year.text: Over the past year Iran went from steady growth into decline. Income per person fell 3.7 percent in 2025 in the data. The World Bank's October 2026 update reports that output shrank in early 2026 and that inflation surged in the months after.

citations.title: Iran, Islamic Republic: Macro Poverty Outlook (October 2026)

citations.title: Iran, Islamic Republic: Macro Poverty Outlook (October 2026)

growth_story.tension: The World Bank describes collapsing investment in 2025/26, but in the data fixed investment rose as a share of GDP, from 25.2 percent in 2019 to 28.1 percent in 2024 and 28.8 percent in 2025. Part of the gap may be timing: the World Bank's year 2025/26 runs to March 2026, past the end of the data's last year.
